en: Vimānavatthu: The Chapter on the Woman’s Vimānas,
Section on the Seats (Pīṭhavagga)
6. The First Mansion of the Ship "O woman,
you stand having boarded a ship with a golden canopy."
"You have entered the lotus pond and are plucking the lotuses with your hand.
By what means do you possess such a complexion?"
By what means do you succeed here?
For all those enjoyments that are dear to the mind arise for you.
I ask you, O goddess of great majesty:
what merit did you perform while being a human being?
By what means have you come to possess such blazing power?
"And your radiance shines in all directions.
Thus questioned by Moggallāna, that deity was uplifted in mind.
When questioned, she explained the deed from which this fruit arises:
"When I was among humans, having become a human being..."
In a previous birth in the human world,
seeing monks who were thirsty and exhausted,
I rose up and gave them water to drink.
Whoever, rising up, gives water to drink to those who are weary and thirsty,
for him there will be rivers of cool water.
Abounding with many garlands and numerous white lotuses,
that river flows around it at all times—
a river of cool water with a bed of sand.
The *ambā* and *sālā* trees, the *tilaka* and *jambu*,
the *uddālaka* and *pāṭali* trees were all in full bloom.
That place was thus endowed with its various grounds.
This most excellent celestial mansion shines with great splendor;
this is the ripening of that very karma here,
for those who have performed merit obtain such a result as this.
Because of that, my complexion is such as this;
because of that, I prosper here;
and wealth arises for me.
"Whatever is dear to the mind—
O monk of great power, I tell you this— those who,
having become human, performed meritorious deeds;"
"Thus I possess such blazing majesty,
and my complexion illuminates all directions.
The first ship-vimāna, the sixth.
